title: A.R.M.O.R. event of the perimeter engine of a radar node
description: One short message a radar node publishes to armor/radar/{node_id}/events (QoS 1, never retained) when its own perimeter engine or one of its sensors finds something: a zone taken or left, a target that stays too long (loiter), a line crossed (tripwire) in one direction, a target that came from where it should not (path_violation), sensors that see nothing while armed (masking), the Wi-Fi jammed, a sensor whose own Bluetooth is open or closed again, the serial bridge to a sensor opened or closed. The words are a fixed list and there is no free text, so nothing secret can be in it. `boot` (random at each start of the node) and `seq` (counting inside that start) identify an event: a server that gets the same pair twice (one sent live and again from the node's memory of an outage) keeps one. A node keeps up to a thousand events in its flash while the broker cannot be reached and sends them in order when it is back.

timestamp_ms.description: The wall-clock time in milliseconds, 0 when the node's clock was not set.

boot.description: A number chosen at random at each start of the node.

seq.description: Counts the events of one start.

name.description: The zone or the line (or the sensor's model, for a Bluetooth event).

movement.description: How the target moves, when the event is about one.

value.description: Seconds (loiter), minutes or a count, according to the event.

count.description: How many targets, when the event counts them.

direction.description: Tripwire: the direction of the crossing.

from.description: Path violation: the zone the target came from, when it came from one.

by.description: Serial bridge: the administrator who opened it.
